Verifier: start_year 2015 comes from the archived NPS release (dave-hallac-selected-as-new-superintendent-for-outer-banks-group.htm, fetched 200): 'He will start his new assignment at Cape Hatteras in early January 2015'.

Division chief Joelle Gore recorded as system-level lead; OCM acting director Keelin Kuipers as parent-office leadership. No named NERRS-specific program manager on fetched pages; individual reserves have their own managers (not in scope here). Verifier: Kuipers downgraded to low confidence (heads the parent office, not NERRS itself).

people.name: David Hallac
people.bio: Superintendent of the National Park Service's eastern North Carolina park group, which comprises Cape Hatteras National Seashore, Fort Raleigh NHS and Wright Brothers National Memorial. Trained in wildlife and fisheries biology at the University of Vermont; earlier work spanned endangered species, wetland restoration, and Everglades estuaries and coral reefs.
people.research_interests: Protected-lands management; ecosystem management and restoration

people.name: Shad Combs
people.bio: Serves as acting head of NASA's Wallops Flight Facility, responsible for executive management and strategic direction of its spaceport and test range. An aerospace engineer with over 25 years in launch and range operations, project management and mission assurance; previously held range and flight-test leadership roles at Wallops and managed a Commercial Access to Space portfolio at NASA Headquarters.

people.name: Joelle Gore
people.bio: Chief of the Stewardship Division in NOAA's Office for Coastal Management, the division that administers the National Estuarine Research Reserve System and national coastal zone programs. At NOAA since 1992; earlier served as acting chief of OCRM's Coastal Programs Division and acting OCRM deputy director. Trained in architecture (UT Austin) and planning (UVA).

people.name: Keelin Kuipers
people.bio: Acting director of NOAA's Office for Coastal Management, formerly its deputy director. Joined NOAA in 1999; past roles include managing the NOAA Coastal Storms Program and serving as resilience lead for NOAA's Coastal Goal, after earlier science-policy work at the National Science Foundation. Graduate training in conservation biology and environmental policy (Michigan).

people.name: Louis (Lou) Licate
people.bio: Center Director of the USGS Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center since 2025, leading its administration and policy. Before USGS he worked at NOAA as an oceanographer and engineering deputy chief at CO-OPS and as a navigation manager in the Office of Coast Survey. Holds master's degrees in oceanography (URI) and physics (Creighton).
people.research_interests: Tides; coastal processes; navigation and nautical charts; science policy and administration

people.name: Nadine Golden
people.bio: Serves as deputy center director at USGS's Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center (Santa Cruz, California); her profile links her to the California Seafloor Mapping Program.

people.name: Guy Gelfenbaum
people.bio: Emeritus oceanographer (since 2022) at USGS's Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center, which he directed from 2017 to 2021. A geological oceanographer (PhD, University of Washington) who led USGS projects on Puget Sound nearshore habitats and southwest Washington coastal erosion and co-led research on tsunami deposits.
people.research_interests: Coastal sediment transport; shoreline erosion and coastal change; nearshore habitats; tsunami deposits and hazards

people.name: Evan Dailey
people.bio: Works as a data management specialist for USGS's Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center in Santa Cruz, California.

people.name: Valerie Paul
people.bio: Head Scientist of the Smithsonian Marine Station at Fort Pierce since 2002. Before joining the Smithsonian she was a professor at the University of Guam Marine Laboratory (1985-2002).

people.name: Mary E. Rice
people.bio: Invertebrate zoologist and National Museum of Natural History curator known for research on sipunculan worms. Founding director of the Smithsonian Marine Station (1981-2002), she planned its 1999 move to a new Fort Pierce laboratory and afterwards held the title of senior research scientist emeritus.
people.research_interests: Sipunculan worms; invertebrate evolution and development
